newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Authorities annul opposition win in Belgrade.
newsitem.headline: Authorities annul opposition win in Belgrade.

text.p: Authorities have cancelled an opposition election victory in the Serbian capital Belgrade, opposition coalition officials said on Sunday.
A municipial court annulled 52 of 60 city council seats previously verifed as won by the opposition in local elections held a week ago, the opposition Democratic party said.
The opposition said it had been informed of the court decision by the local electoral commission.
"This is proof that power cannot be won in Serbia by elections, that power is won by robbery," Zoran Djindjic, one of the Zajedno (Together) coalition leaders, told Reuters

"We have now been brought to a dramatic situation in which all citizens are becoming aware that the regime in Serbia cannot be changed by elections and cannot be changed legally but only in another way -- illegally, by uprisings, strikes, violence".

Other opposition leaders, speaking on the city's only independent radio station, called for civil disobedience to protest what it called massive fraud committed by the ruling Socialists of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.
Local electoral authorities declined to comment to reporters
The move was sure to provoke an angry reaction from oppposition folllowers who have taken to the streets in the past week to urge authorities to confirm Zajedno victories in 15 other major towns.
Zajedno said it won 70 seats in the 110-seat city council to capture the capital in run-off polls, in a stunning blow to Milosevic who has ruled the country with an iron first for nine years.
In towns where the opposition said it prevailed, local electoral commissions have either failed to announce final results or annulled results or ordered another round of voting.
Opposition demonstrations over the past five days have drawn tens of thousands of people in Belgrade and major industrial centres in the biggest streets protests in three years.
